__PART A — THE CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER__

__1–5   Category 1: Strategic Financial Planning & Decision Support__

__ \#1   Annual Operating Plan & Three\-Year Financial Roadmap__

▶ __Use Case: __Translate the board's strategic direction into a rigorous, defensible operating plan and three\-year roadmap\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are acting as the CFO of \[COMPANY\], a \[INDUSTRY\] business with ₹\[X\] crore of annual revenue\. The board has approved a strategic direction comprising: \(1\) \[GROWTH INITIATIVE 1\], \(2\) \[GROWTH INITIATIVE 2\], and \(3\) \[EFFICIENCY/MARGIN INITIATIVE\]\. Translate this into a board\-ready Annual Operating Plan \(AOP\) for FY\[YEAR\] and a supporting three\-year financial roadmap\.

For each strategic initiative build a financial section covering: the revenue ramp \(Year 1: 25% of run\-rate, Year 2: 70%, Year 3: 100%\), the gross\-margin profile of the incremental revenue, the upfront investment \(capex, hiring, launch, approvals\), the cash break\-even expressed in months, and the EBITDA sensitivity to a 15% revenue shortfall\. Then produce a consolidated three\-statement view \(P&L, balance sheet, cash flow\) for each year, splitting ‘base business’ from ‘new initiatives’ so the board sees both the organic trajectory and the growth investment separately\. Identify the peak\-funding year and the debt or equity required to bridge it\. Close with the three questions the board is most likely to ask and the specific financial data you would cite to answer each\. State every assumption explicitly and flag the three assumptions that most influence the outcome\.

__✓ Expected Output: __AOP with initiative\-level financials, consolidated three\-statement three\-year plan \(base vs new\-initiative split\), peak\-funding requirement, key\-assumption register, and three board Q&A points\.

__ \#2   Rolling 12\-Month Forecast — Design & Governance__

▶ __Use Case: __Replace a static annual budget with a dynamic rolling forecast that stays current and frees up FP&A capacity\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO designing a Rolling Forecast process for \[COMPANY\]\. The current annual budget takes \[N\] weeks, goes stale within 60 days, and consumes roughly \[X\]% of FP&A capacity\. Design a complete rolling\-forecast operating model\.

Cover: \(1\) Horizon & Cadence — choose a 12, 15 or 18\-month forward view and justify it against \[COMPANY\]’s capital\-commitment lead times; \(2\) Driver Architecture — identify the 8–12 business drivers that explain 85%\+ of revenue and cost variability without bottom\-up line\-item input; for each, name the owner, the update frequency, and the external data source that validates it; \(3\) Scenario Management — how to carry Base, Upside and Downside simultaneously without tripling the workload; \(4\) Governance — who prepares, who challenges, and who approves each update at BU, finance and executive level; \(5\) Incentive Interaction — how rolling targets coexist with the annual bonus plan so removing a fixed budget does not create gaming\. Add a change\-management plan \(likely BU objections, FP&A training, Excel vs dedicated planning tool\) and a 90\-day implementation roadmap\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Rolling\-forecast design covering horizon, driver architecture, scenario management, governance, incentive interaction, change\-management plan, and 90\-day roadmap\.

__ \#3   Scenario & Stress\-Test Modelling__

▶ __Use Case: __Prepare the organisation financially for three distinct macro regimes and define early\-warning triggers\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\]\. The environment is uncertain: interest rates may ease, hold or rise; your two largest customers sit in cyclical industries; and your cost base is exposed to \[INPUT/WAGE\] inflation\. Build a formal scenario\-planning framework for the next 18 months\.

Define three scenarios with full macro context: A — Soft Landing \(\[GDP/CPI/rate path\]\); B — Sticky Inflation \(\[path\], margin pressure intensifying\); C — Downturn \(\[contraction\], project deferrals, tighter credit, possible covenant pressure\)\. For each, model revenue \(by segment, reflecting customer sensitivity\), gross margin \(input cost and pricing\), free cash flow \(working\-capital swings\), the balance sheet \(covenant headroom\), and the liquidity runway\. For Scenario C build a cash\-preservation playbook: which costs are cut first, which capex is deferred, which hiring is frozen, which collections are accelerated\. For each scenario define 3–5 leading indicators the CFO monitors monthly, with explicit trigger levels that activate the playbook\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Three\-scenario 18\-month model \(P&L, FCF, balance sheet\), Scenario C cash\-preservation playbook, and leading\-indicator dashboard with trigger levels\.

__ \#4   Capital Expenditure Appraisal & Prioritisation__

▶ __Use Case: __Bring discipline to capex decisions and rank competing projects on a consistent value basis\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] facing ₹\[X\] crore of capex requests against an approved envelope of ₹\[Y\] crore\. Design a capex appraisal and prioritisation framework and apply it to the \[N\] largest requests: \[LIST\]\.

For each project compute: payback, NPV and IRR at the company WACC of \[Z\]%, and the value at risk under a downside case\. Classify each as Maintenance / Mandatory \(safety, regulatory, contractual\), Cost\-Saving \(quantified efficiency\), or Growth \(new capacity/markets\)\. Build a single ranking that maximises value within the envelope, showing which projects make the cut and which are deferred, and the EBITDA/ROCE impact of the approved portfolio\. Define the post\-approval governance: stage\-gates, the threshold above which board approval is required, and the post\-implementation review that compares realised vs business\-case returns\. State the three projects whose ranking is most sensitive to the WACC assumption\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Capex appraisal framework, project\-level NPV/IRR/payback, a prioritised portfolio within the envelope, governance and stage\-gate design, and a post\-implementation review template\.

__ \#5   Corporate KPI / Value\-Driver Tree Design__

▶ __Use Case: __Connect operational activity to financial outcomes and shareholder value through a lean KPI architecture\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO redesigning \[COMPANY\]’s KPI framework\. The current dashboard has \[N\] metrics reported monthly — information overload, no clear accountability, and someone can always find a flattering number\. Design a lean, high\-accountability framework from first principles\.

Step 1 — Value\-Driver Tree: start from Enterprise Value ≈ FCF / \(WACC − g\); decompose FCF into EBITDA × FCF conversion − capex; decompose EBITDA into Revenue × EBITDA margin; keep decomposing until each leaf is owned and directly actionable by a function or BU\. Cap the tree at 3–4 levels and ≤20 leaf nodes\. Step 2 — Primary KPIs: select 8–10 metrics that, if all on track, virtually guarantee plan delivery; for each state the metric, the owner, the monthly target, and the variance band before intervention\. Step 3 — Leading vs Lagging: ensure a balance of predictive \(pipeline, satisfaction, engagement\) and confirmatory \(revenue, margin, FCF\) measures\. Step 4 — Cascade: show how the primary KPIs cascade to department KPIs for Sales, Operations and Finance\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Value\-driver tree, 8–10 primary KPIs with owner/target/variance band, leading\-vs\-lagging balance, and a department\-level cascade for three functions\.

__6–10   Category 2: Board, Audit Committee & Stakeholder Communication__

__ \#6   Monthly Board Financial Report__

▶ __Use Case: __Produce a concise board report that drives decisions rather than merely reporting history\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO preparing \[COMPANY\]’s monthly board financial report for \[MONTH\] \[YEAR\]\. The board mixes financially\-literate directors and industry/strategic directors, so the report must be rigorous yet clear\. Target length: 8–10 pages plus appendix\.

Page 1 — Executive Summary: a three\-line scorecard \(Revenue / EBITDA / FCF\) actual vs plan vs prior year, for the month and YTD; three commentary bullets \(revenue, cost/margin, cash\) each opening with the conclusion not the data; and the one decision the board must take or ratify\. Pages 2–3 — Revenue: by segment/product/geography, with a volume\-price\-mix bridge and pipeline health\. Pages 4–5 — Cost & Margin: gross\-margin bridge vs prior year, opex waterfall, headcount vs plan\. Pages 6–7 — Cash & Balance Sheet: 13\-week cash forecast, working\-capital movement, covenant status, near\-term liquidity\. Page 8 — Risks & Opportunities: top three risks and top two opportunities, each with probability, financial impact and recommended response\. Appendix: full three\-statement actuals\.

Writing standards: every chart title states the conclusion \(e\.g\. ‘Gross margin fell 180 bps as input costs outpaced price’, not ‘Gross margin trend’\); every variance states cause, magnitude and whether it reverses; no vanity metrics\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Full 8\-page board report structure with executive summary, revenue, cost/margin, cash and balance sheet, risks/opportunities, and writing standards per section\.

__ \#7   Audit Committee Pack & Engagement Framework__

▶ __Use Case: __Build an effective Audit Committee communication framework aligned to Section 177 of the Companies Act, 2013\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO managing \[COMPANY\]’s Audit Committee \(constituted under Section 177 of the Companies Act, 2013 and, if listed, SEBI LODR Regulation 18\)\. Design the full\-year engagement framework\.

Channel 1 — Quarterly Agenda \(2\.5 hours\): \(a\) private session with the statutory auditor \(no management\); \(b\) private session with internal audit; \(c\) CFO financial update — results, accounting judgements, open items; \(d\) statutory\-audit update — progress, significant findings, going\-concern view; \(e\) internal\-audit update — plan progress, findings, remediation status; \(f\) critical accounting estimates and Ind AS judgements with sensitivity; \(g\) related\-party transactions and approvals; \(h\) other business\. Channel 2 — Pre\-read \(circulated 5 working days ahead\): CFO materials \(2–3 pages\), auditor materials, internal\-audit materials, fronted by a one\-page ‘five things to focus on this quarter’\. Channel 3 — Between\-meeting protocol: which events need immediate notification \(suspected fraud, regulator inquiry, restatement being evaluated, material weakness\) versus next\-meeting reporting; and the CFO’s direct cadence with the Audit Committee Chair\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Audit Committee framework with a Section 177\-aligned quarterly agenda, pre\-read standards, escalation protocol, and Chair\-communication cadence\.

__ \#8   Lender / Banker Information Pack & Covenant Reporting__

▶ __Use Case: __Maintain lender confidence through disciplined, proactive financial reporting and covenant management\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\], which carries ₹\[X\] crore of debt across \[a working\-capital facility / term loan / NCDs\] with \[N\] lenders and the following covenants: \[LIST — e\.g\. DSCR ≥ \[a\], Net Debt/EBITDA ≤ \[b\], current ratio ≥ \[c\]\]\. Design the standard lender information pack and covenant\-reporting process\.

Build: \(1\) a quarterly covenant compliance certificate showing each covenant’s definition, the computed value, the headroom, and the EBITDA decline that would breach the tightest covenant; \(2\) a one\-page lender summary — performance vs plan, liquidity, order book, and any item the lender should hear from you first; \(3\) a 13\-week cash\-flow view for the working\-capital lender; \(4\) an early\-warning protocol — the metrics that, if they move, trigger a proactive lender call before a breach\. Add the communication principle: share good news early and bad news faster, and never let a lender be surprised\. Draft the covering note for the quarterly submission\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Lender pack with covenant compliance certificate \(with headroom and breach sensitivity\), one\-page summary, 13\-week cash view, early\-warning protocol, and a covering note\.

__ \#9   Investor / Promoter Capital\-Allocation Narrative__

▶ __Use Case: __Articulate how capital is being deployed and the returns it is generating, for investors or promoters\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] preparing the capital\-allocation narrative for \[the AGM / an investor update / the promoter group\]\. Build a financially honest story that connects deployment to value creation\.

Element 1 — Capital Allocation Track Record: review every significant decision over the last three years \(capex, acquisitions, buybacks, dividends, debt reduction\); for each state the amount deployed, the expected return, and — critically — whether early evidence suggests the assumption was right\. Intellectual honesty about one decision tracking below plan builds more credibility than glossing over it\. Element 2 — Return on Capital: present ROCE/ROIC versus the cost of capital for the last five years and the forward three, showing whether the spread is positive and widening\. Element 3 — Cash Generation Quality: show FCF conversion \(FCF / PAT\) over three years as evidence of earnings quality\. Element 4 — Forward Priorities: state the priority order for the next rupee of capital \(organic > inorganic > debt reduction > distribution, or your order\), the return hurdle for each use, and the conditions that would change the priority\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Capital\-allocation narrative with a three\-year track record \(including an honest miss\), five\-year ROCE\-vs\-WACC spread, FCF conversion history, and a forward capital\-priority framework\.

__ \#10   Management Discussion & Analysis \(MD&A\) Drafting__

▶ __Use Case: __Draft a substantive MD&A for the annual report that is candid and decision\-useful, not boilerplate\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO drafting the Management Discussion & Analysis section of \[COMPANY\]’s FY\[YEAR\] annual report\. Results: Revenue ₹\[X\] crore \(\+\[Y\]%\), EBITDA margin \[Z\]%, PAT ₹\[W\] crore, and ₹\[V\] crore returned to shareholders\. The year was shaped by \[KEY DEVELOPMENT\]\.

Structure: \(1\) Economic and industry context relevant to the business; \(2\) Segment\-wise operational and financial performance with specific, verifiable drivers; \(3\) Financial review — a clear bridge of the major year\-on\-year movements in revenue, margin and PAT, each with cause, magnitude and whether it persists; \(4\) Balance sheet, liquidity and capital structure; \(5\) Risks and concerns with the mitigation in place; \(6\) Internal control adequacy statement; \(7\) Outlook framed as priorities with measurable outcomes, not aspiration\. Apply these standards: avoid boilerplate \(‘we are pleased to report’\), quantify every claim, and name the one or two areas that fell short of internal expectations and what has changed operationally\. Comply with the SEBI LODR disclosure expectations for MD&A where the company is listed\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Full MD&A draft across seven sections with quantified bridges, an honest underperformance discussion, internal\-control statement, and a measurable outlook\.

__11–15   Category 3: Capital Allocation, Funding & M&A__

__ \#11   Financial Due Diligence Workplan \(Quality of Earnings\)__

▶ __Use Case: __Build a comprehensive financial due\-diligence plan to support a confident go/no\-go on an acquisition\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO leading financial due diligence on \[TARGET\], a ₹\[X\] crore revenue business in \[INDUSTRY\] being evaluated at an enterprise value of ₹\[Y\] crore\. The team has \[N\] weeks\. Design the complete workplan\.

Workstream 1 — Quality of Earnings: verify that reported EBITDA is real, recurring and sustainable; scrutinise every management add\-back and classify it legitimate or aggressive; compute your own ‘True EBITDA’ removing wishful synergies and including all genuine recurring costs; flag revenue\-recognition policies that pull future revenue forward\. Workstream 2 — Revenue & Customer Quality: analyse the top 20 customers \(concentration, churn, contract terms, renewal probability\) and build an independent Year\-1 revenue model from contracts, not management projections\. Workstream 3 — Working\-Capital Normalisation: determine ‘normal’ working capital and the average seasonal level, and identify any period\-end window\-dressing\. Workstream 4 — Capex: split maintenance from growth capex and test whether reported capex sustains current revenue\. Workstream 5 — Liabilities: map on\- and off\-balance\-sheet liabilities — contingent claims, tax disputes, gratuity/leave obligations, lease commitments, and unpaid statutory dues\. End each workstream with the key red flags and the go/no\-go criteria\.

__✓ Expected Output: __FDD workplan across QoE, revenue quality, working\-capital normalisation, capex and liabilities — each with red flags and go/no\-go criteria\.

__ \#12   Capital Structure Optimisation & Cost of Capital__

▶ __Use Case: __Find the debt\-equity balance that minimises the cost of capital and supports the strategy\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO assessing whether \[COMPANY\]’s capital structure \(Net Debt/EBITDA of \[X\]x, credit rating \[RATING\], EBITDA ₹\[A\] crore, FCF ₹\[B\] crore\) is optimal\. Conduct a full optimisation analysis\.

Section 1 — Current WACC: compute cost of equity via CAPM and after\-tax cost of debt from the actual borrowing cost; judge whether the company is under\-levered \(cheap debt capacity unused\) or over\-levered \(distress cost exceeding the tax shield\)\. Section 2 — Leverage Capacity: for credit\-rating bands appropriate to \[INDUSTRY\], compute the maximum sustainable debt at each level and, for each leverage scenario, the WACC, the incremental interest, the resulting equity cash flow, and the implied value per share at a constant EV/EBITDA multiple\. Section 3 — Optimal Structure: identify the leverage that minimises WACC and maximises value per share and present a sensitivity table\. Section 4 — Path: design a 24\-month route to the target — issuance plus buyback if under\-levered, or an FCF sweep if over\-levered\. Section 5 — Rate Sensitivity: given \[X\]% floating\-rate debt, compute the FCF and EPS impact of \+100 and \+200 bps\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Capital\-structure analysis with current WACC, leverage\-capacity\-by\-rating table, value\-per\-share sensitivity, optimal\-structure identification, a 24\-month path, and rate sensitivity\.

__ \#13   Debt Raising / Refinancing & Banking Strategy__

▶ __Use Case: __Optimise the debt portfolio and refinancing timeline in the current rate environment\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO assessing \[COMPANY\]’s debt: \(a\) a ₹\[X\] crore working\-capital facility at \[rate\] with covenants \[LIST\]; \(b\) ₹\[A\] crore term loan at \[rate\] maturing \[DATE\]; \(c\) ₹\[C\] crore of NCDs at \[rate\] maturing \[DATE\]\. Evaluate the optimal near\- and long\-term strategy\.

\(1\) Facility adequacy — test the worst\-case 13\-week cash burn against available limits and headroom above minimum operating cash\. \(2\) Pricing — compare current spreads to the market for \[COMPANY\]’s credit profile and estimate the saving from a repricing or lender switch, with the NPV of interest saved\. \(3\) Maturity\-wall analysis — build a five\-year maturity calendar, flag any cluster of maturities within a 12\-month window that creates refinancing risk, and design a proactive timeline addressing each maturity 12–18 months ahead\. \(4\) Mix — recommend the target fixed/floating split and whether to lock longer\-tenor fixed debt now\. \(5\) Rating/lender management — the metrics rating agencies and key lenders focus on and the specific actions that protect or improve the profile\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Debt strategy covering facility adequacy, repricing NPV, a five\-year maturity calendar with cliff analysis, a fixed/floating recommendation, and a rating/lender management plan\.

__ \#14   Working Capital Optimisation Programme__

▶ __Use Case: __Release cash from operations by systematically compressing the cash\-conversion cycle\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] with a cash\-conversion cycle of \[X\] days — \[Y\] days above the industry median\. Growth of \[G\]% is consuming ₹\[Z\] crore of additional working capital a year\. Design a programme to cut the CCC by \[W\] days within 18 months\.

Workstream 1 — Receivables \(DSO\): set the target DSO; identify the top drivers \(invoicing errors, customer behaviour, weak collections\); design interventions — e\-invoicing with reminders at day 15/30/45, an early\-payment discount for large customers \(compute the discount cost against the cash\-acceleration benefit at the company cost of capital\), and an ageing dashboard by customer and collector\. Workstream 2 — Inventory \(DIO\): analyse raw material, WIP and finished goods days; separate justified buffers \(long lead time, seasonal\) from unjustified \(poor planning, slow\-moving SKUs\); run a monthly SKU\-rationalisation and liquidation of slow stock before obsolescence\. Workstream 3 — Payables \(DPO\): compare DPO to terms and the median; identify term\-extension opportunities \(with supplier\-relationship cost weighed against the cash benefit\) and evaluate supply\-chain finance\. Quantify total CCC reduction and cash released\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Working\-capital programme for receivables, inventory and payables with specific interventions, early\-payment\-discount NPV, and quantified CCC reduction and cash release\.

__ \#15   Build vs Buy vs Partner Financial Evaluation__

▶ __Use Case: __Compare three routes into a new capability or market on a rigorous, consistent financial basis\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO evaluating three routes for \[COMPANY\] to enter \[CAPABILITY/MARKET\]: \(1\) Build — invest ₹\[X\] crore over \[Y\] years organically; \(2\) Acquire — buy \[TARGET\] at an EV of ₹\[Z\] crore; \(3\) Partner/License — a ₹\[W\] crore annual fee plus \[%\] revenue share\.

Compare across five dimensions: \(1\) Time to Revenue — the earliest date each route reaches ₹\[threshold\] crore of incremental annual revenue, and the NPV value of earlier revenue; \(2\) Total Investment — five\-year committed capital including upfront cost, ongoing investment and the opportunity cost of management and engineering bandwidth; \(3\) Revenue Upside — the best\-case Year\-5 contribution under each \(Build assumes full product\-market fit; Buy assumes distribution synergy; Partner is capped by the terms\); \(4\) Risk — score execution risk, credibility risk and financial\-loss risk 1–5 each and weight them; \(5\) NPV/IRR — a five\-year DCF at the company WACC, with base, upside and downside\. Conclude with a recommendation, the financial rationale, and the three conditions under which it would change\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Build vs Buy vs Partner comparison across five dimensions with three\-scenario NPV per route and a recommendation with change conditions\.

__16–20   Category 4: Financial Reporting, Controls & Compliance__

__ \#16   Month\-End Close Acceleration Programme__

▶ __Use Case: __Cut the close cycle so the leadership team decides on fresh, not stale, numbers\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] where the monthly close takes \[N\] business days — several days slower than peers of similar complexity — so decisions rest on data nearly three weeks old\. Design a programme to reach a \[T\]\-business\-day close within 90 days\.

Phase 1 — Diagnostic: map every close activity with owner, duration, dependency and critical\-path status; surface the top five bottlenecks \(likely: intercompany reconciliation, manual journals, revenue cut\-off, inventory valuation, consolidation\)\. Phase 2 — Quick wins \(days 1–30\): move fixed accruals, recurring journals and depreciation to a soft close in the last week of the month; automate any fixed or simple\-calculation journal; set a ‘no post\-close adjustment below ₹\[threshold\]’ materiality rule\. Phase 3 — Redesign \(days 31–60\): automate intercompany matching daily rather than at month\-end; deploy account\-reconciliation tooling; standardise the subsidiary submission file\. Phase 4 — Governance \(days 61–90\): a close calendar with named owners and due\-times, a daily 15\-minute close stand\-up, and an escalation path for slipping items\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Close\-acceleration programme with diagnostic, quick wins, process redesign and governance phases, targeting the stated cycle\-time reduction\.

__ \#17   Internal Financial Controls \(IFC\) Framework__

▶ __Use Case: __Design or strengthen an IFC framework that satisfies Section 134/143 of the Companies Act, 2013\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] designing the Internal Financial Controls over financial reporting framework required under the Companies Act, 2013 \(the board’s responsibility statement under Section 134\(5\)\(e\) and the auditor’s reporting under Section 143\(3\)\(i\)\)\. Build a comprehensive programme\.

Section 1 — Scoping: identify the in\-scope entities, financial\-statement line items and processes by quantitative and qualitative significance, and document the rationale for any exclusions\. Section 2 — Risk & Control Matrix: for each key process \(Revenue/Order\-to\-Cash, Procure\-to\-Pay, Inventory, Financial Close & Reporting, Payroll, Treasury, IT General Controls\) identify what could go wrong, the key control mitigating each risk, and whether the control is manual or automated; mark the ‘key controls’ whose failure no other control would catch\. Section 3 — Documentation: the standard for each control — description \(what/who/when/how\), population, evidence of operation, and testing approach\. Section 4 — Testing: risk\-based frequency \(quarterly/half\-yearly/annual\) concentrating effort on the highest\-risk processes\. Section 5 — Deficiencies: define control deficiency, significant deficiency and material weakness, with remediation timelines and Audit Committee reporting for each\.

__✓ Expected Output: __IFC framework with scoping rationale, a risk\-and\-control matrix for the key processes, documentation standards, a risk\-based testing plan, and deficiency\-management protocol\.

__ \#18   Ind AS Accounting Position Paper & Disclosure__

▶ __Use Case: __Document a defensible accounting position on a complex or judgemental transaction\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] preparing an accounting position paper on \[TRANSACTION/ISSUE — e\.g\. revenue recognition on a multi\-element contract under Ind AS 115, a lease classification under Ind AS 116, an expected\-credit\-loss provision under Ind AS 109, a business combination under Ind AS 103, or an impairment under Ind AS 36\]\. The paper must withstand statutory\-auditor and Audit Committee scrutiny\.

Structure: \(1\) Facts — the transaction, the contractual terms and the commercial substance; \(2\) Issue — the specific recognition, measurement or disclosure question; \(3\) Standards — the relevant Ind AS paragraphs and the recognition/measurement principles they set; \(4\) Analysis — apply the principles to the facts, set out the alternatives genuinely available, and explain why the chosen treatment best reflects substance; \(5\) Judgements & Estimates — the key assumptions and the sensitivity of the reported number to each; \(6\) Conclusion — the accounting entries and the P&L/balance\-sheet impact; \(7\) Disclosure — the note language for the financial statements\. Flag where the position is finely balanced and where an auditor might reasonably take a different view\.

__✓ Expected Output: __Ind AS position paper with facts, issue, standards, reasoned analysis of alternatives, key judgements with sensitivity, accounting entries, and draft disclosure note\.

__ \#19   Statutory & Tax Compliance Calendar__

▶ __Use Case: __Build a single, owner\-assigned compliance calendar across GST, TDS, Income Tax, ROC and labour laws\.

● __CLAUDE PROMPT__

You are the CFO of \[COMPANY\] consolidating fragmented compliance into one governed calendar covering GST, TDS/TCS, Income Tax, Companies Act/ROC filings, and applicable labour and other statutory obligations for FY\[YEAR\]\.

Produce a month\-by\-month calendar listing, for each obligation: the return or filing, the governing law and section, the statutory due date, the named owner, the maker\-checker reviewer, and the consequence of delay \(interest, late fee, penalty, disqualification\)\. Include the recurring monthly items \(GSTR\-1, GSTR\-3B, TDS payment and returns, PF/ESI\), the periodic items \(advance tax instalments, GST annual return and reconciliation, tax audit, ROC annual filings, board\-meeting and secretarial compliances\), and event\-based triggers\.
